title: Chapter 123 — The Leader's Scorecard
intro: The metrics, rhythms, and reviews that define leadership performance.

sections.title: What Leaders Measure
sections.content:
Sales leaders are measured on team performance, not personal production. The scorecard shifts from 'how much did I sell' to 'how much did my team sell — and is each member improving?'

The leader's scorecard: total team revenue versus budget. Revenue per rep — who is producing and who needs support. Team close rate — overall and by rep. Team attach rate — overall and by rep. Employee retention — are you keeping your best people? Training completion — is the team developing? Customer satisfaction — reviews, complaint rate, NPS.

sections.title: The Review Cadence
sections.content:
Daily: check the sales board. Who sold? Who did not? Any delivery issues?

Weekly: 15-minute one-on-ones with each rep. Team meeting with wins, focus, and training. Pipeline review — who has open quotes and are they following up?

Monthly: scorecard review. P&L analysis. Identify trends — what is improving, what is declining, and why. Coach the specific gaps.

Quarterly: business review with ownership or regional management. Strategic planning for the next quarter. Account reviews for trade business. Training curriculum updates.

sections.title: The Compound Effect of Consistent Leadership
sections.content:
A five-minute huddle every day is 20 hours of coaching per year delivered in doses small enough that people absorb it. That is more effective than any annual training event.

A 15-minute one-on-one every week is 13 hours per rep per year of focused development. Multiply by 8 reps and you are investing 104 hours in team development — the equivalent of 13 full working days dedicated to making your team better.

This is how 10 percent improvements in each metric compound into 45 percent overall growth. Not through motivation or intensity — through consistent, rhythmic, systematic leadership.
